source.section: Schedule 2 lines 5 and 6 (PDF page 17 Lines 5 and 6: 'Indiana does not tax Social Security income or the railroad retirement benefits'); PDF page 23 Code 630; Schedule 3 line 1 (PDF page 24: joint 2,000, all other filers 1,000), line 4 (PDF page 25: 1,000 age 65 or older), line 5 (PDF page 25: 500 age 65 or older and IT-40 line 1 under 40,000, or under 20,000 married filing separately); Form IT-40 lines 1-8 (PDF page 1; line 8 'multiply line 7 by 3% (.03)'); booklet PDF page 8 Line 1; PDF pages 5-6 rounding

worked: Federal AGI = private pension person 0 40,000.00 + taxable Social Security 22,350.00 = 62,350.00. Social Security received: person 0 30,000.00; the federal taxable amount from the federal worksheet is 22,350.00. Federal taxable income = 62,350.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 additional = 44,600.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored; Indiana starts from federal AGI). Form IT-40 line 1 federal AGI 62,350.00. Line 2 add-backs 0.00; line 3 = 62,350.00 + 0.00 = 62,350.00. Schedule 2: line 5 taxable Social Security 22,350.00; line 12 total = 22,350.00. IT-40 line 4 = 22,350.00. Line 5 = 62,350.00 - 22,350.00 = 40,000.00. Schedule 3: line 1 1,000.00; line 4 1 x 1,000.00 = 1,000.00; line 5 IT-40 line 1 62,350.00 is not less than 40,000.00: none; line 7 total = 2,000.00. IT-40 line 6 = 2,000.00. Line 7 = 40,000.00 - 2,000.00 = 38,000.00. Line 8 = 38,000.00 x 0.03 = 1,140.00. No credits; county tax (line 9) is local and out of scope. State income tax 1,140.00. Only the federal taxable amount is in federal AGI, so that is what Schedule 2 line 5 takes out. The 500 is lost because federal AGI is over 40,000 even though line 5 is 40,000.00.
